purpose: Validate tcpcc on the target constrained OpenVZ deployment class and record throughput, CPU, RSS, and OpenVZ physical-page accounting.

provenance.limitation: The original field run recorded Linux 6.18.49-dirty and related PR state, but not an immutable tcpcc source commit. Treat this snapshot as an operational observation, not a release benchmark.

tcpcc_cubic.note: Several adjacent runs were broadly normal, but the public path also produced severe outliers.

tcpcc_bbr.note: Bad runs correlated with severe memory pressure in at least some 128 MiB observations; later experiments also proved that the WAN path itself could independently collapse.

interpretation: tcpcc successfully booted and served public TCP on the intended 128 MiB OpenVZ deployment class even though the tenant could not select host TCP congestion control.
The 128 MiB guest arena was demand-backed rather than permanently resident at 128 MiB.
CPU was not the limiting resource in the observed high-throughput run.
The public WAN path was non-stationary; throughput values from this observation must not be used as a controlled native-vs-tcpcc speedup claim.
Follow-up work corrected the temporary tcp_wmem/tcp_mem policy mismatch and preserved upstream Linux RAM-derived TCP memory policy by default.
